protein: Tgo-D4K (engineered FANA polymerase)
readout: FANA synthesis rate, normalized to the Tgo-D4K parent (fold)
assay_method: Polymerase kinetic profiling (PKPro). 20 nM polymerase, 1 uM 30-mer DNA template, 100 uM each NTP, 1x ThermoPol buffer, 2x LC Green Plus; denature 95 degC 3 min, extend 55 degC 30 min, fluorescence every 6 s; rate from a linear fit of nucleotides per polymerase vs time; mean of three independent replicates.
remark: No WT row: the readout is already normalized to the Tgo-D4K parent, which is 1.0 by definition. The reference sequence is the engineered Tgo-D4K parent, not native Tgo. Position 659 follows the source data, which carries Y and lists the variant as Y659E; the paper text instead calls it H659E. Q93A is listed twice with values differing by 7e-5, and the mean is used.

protein: IFRS (pyrrolysyl-tRNA synthetase MmPylRS N346I/C348S, charges 3-bromo-Phe onto tRNA-Pyl for amber suppression)
readout: Stop codon suppression efficiency, normalized to the IFRS parent (fold)
assay_method: Amber suppression of sfGFP-S2TAG in E. coli co-expressing the PylRS variant (glnS promoter) and PylT (lpp promoter) with 3-bromo-Phe (3BrF). Cells grown to OD600 0.4-0.6, resuspended in minimal medium, induced with 0.2 percent arabinose, 12 h at 37 degC; fluorescence on a BioTek Synergy H1 (ex/em 485/515 nm), background-corrected and divided by OD600; the Flu/OD of cells cultured without ncAA is subtracted, and the result divided by the parent measured alongside. Triplicate in Fig. 1b, 1c, 1e, 1g, 2c, 2f, 2h and Supplementary Fig. 6; a single value in the Fig. 2b and 2d screens and the Fig. 2g test set.
remark: The reference sequence is IFRS, MmPylRS translated from the supplementary DNA (Supplementary Data Table 1) with the paper's own specificity mutations N346I/C348S applied, and otherwise identical to UniProt Q8PWY1. There is no WT row, the parent reading 1.0 by definition rather than by measurement, and each readout is the mean of its panel's replicates after collapsing variants appearing in more than one panel, the worst disagreement being K67R at 0.527 in Fig. 2d against 0.801 in Fig. 2b, where the Fig. 2d value is taken; the wild-type sfGFP control of Fig. 2h and the parent-residue cells of the Fig. 2d landscape are not variants and are dropped. The second engineering round is reported against Com1-IFRS and is rebased onto the IFRS scale by that parent's own value of 11.1247, with every label re-derived from the assembled sequence so that substitutions landing on the seven positions Com1-IFRS already carries compose rather than duplicate, which leaves the two rounds joined at that single genotype and nowhere else; Fig. 2h is converted from normalized fluorescence by the Com1-IFRS mean of that panel and its Z7-n labels expanded through Supplementary Table 8. protein: McbA, an ATP-dependent amide synthetase that couples a carboxylic acid and an amine
readout: Percent conversion to moclobemide, as a fold change against wild-type McbA
assay_method: Cell-free DNA assembly and cell-free gene expression of each McbA variant, followed by a functional assay reading percent conversion of the amine and acid substrates to the amide product by LC-MS, normalized to wild-type McbA measured on the same plate. Site-saturation hot-spot screen across 64 residues, n = 1 per variant.
remark: The reference sequence is the assayed construct, Strep-II- and TEV-tagged McbA translated from the supplementary DNA, and residue numbering follows that construct rather than the mature enzyme; after the 23-residue tag it is identical to UniProt R4R1U5 at 494 of 495 positions, the exception being the initiator methionine replaced by the glycine the TEV site leaves behind, and all 64 screened positions verify against it. The screen measures the parent once at every one of the 64 positions rather than defining it as 1, so the WT row is the mean of those 64 measurements, which themselves span 0.688 to 1.215 and are the clearest available statement of the assay's reproducibility at n = 1. Empty cells are dropped. Not extracted from this paper: the four-site combinatorial training and test libraries deposited on GitHub, which measure a different library on the same enzyme; the zero-shot prediction tables, which are computed rather than assayed; and the Fig. 2b substrate scope, which varies the reaction rather than the protein.

protein: ParLQ, a protoglobin engineered for non-native carbene transfer; it is ParPgb carrying W59L and Y60Q, and the construct includes a C-terminal LE-His6 tag
readout: Yield of the cis-2a cyclopropane product (percent)
assay_method: Whole-cell cyclopropanation of styrene with ethyl diazoacetate in 96-well plate format, product quantified by chromatography against an internal standard; five active-site residues (56, 57, 59, 60, 89) were randomized and variants identified by evSeq. Parent and 395 variants across an initial site-saturation set and two rounds of active-learning-selected combinations.
remark: The reference sequence is ParLQ translated from the supplementary DNA of Table S1, 199 residues including the C-terminal LE-His6 tag, and positions 56, 57, 59, 60 and 89 read WYLQF, matching the parent code the source data uses; no UniProt entry for ParPgb was found, so the sequence rests on the supplement alone. Variants are named in the source by a five-letter code over the randomized sites and are converted to substitution labels against the parent, a code letter equal to the parent residue contributing nothing; the parent's own code WYLQF becomes the WT row. The readout is the source's cis-2a yield column as it stands. Not extracted from this paper: the trans-2a yield on its own, which the source provides but which has no higher-is-better orientation, since the paper treats more trans product as worse rather than better; the plate-normalized ALDE objective, which is a restatement of the same pair of yields; and the public benchmark landscapes the paper runs simulations on, which belong to the publications that measured them.

protein: pCNF-RS, a Methanocaldococcus jannaschii tyrosyl-tRNA synthetase engineered to charge p-cyanophenylalanine
readout: Amber suppression activity as a fold change against wild-type pCNF-RS
assay_method: Fluorescence of a sfGFP amber-suppression reporter in E. coli, built and screened by an automated biofoundry in 96-well format, with fitness computed against the activity of wild-type pCNF-RS. Four rounds of 96 variants each: an ESM-2 zero-shot selection followed by three rounds chosen by a multilayer-perceptron fitness predictor retrained on the accumulated data.
remark: The reference sequence is pCNF-RS as given in the supplementary information, 306 residues, which differs from wild-type MjTyrRS (UniProt Q57834) at the six specificity positions Y32L, L65V, F108W, Q109M, D158G and I159A and reads HPMD at the four randomized positions 283 to 286, matching the code the source data uses for the wild type. Variants are named in the source by a four-letter code over those positions and are converted to substitution labels against the parent, a letter equal to the parent residue contributing nothing. There is no WT row: the library did not sample the parent code HPMD, and the readout is defined against wild-type pCNF-RS, which is 1.0 by that definition rather than by measurement. Not extracted from this paper: the UBC9 and ubiquitin benchmark landscapes in Supplementary Data 1, which were measured by other publications and belong to them.

protein: SpCas9, the Streptococcus pyogenes CRISPR-associated endonuclease; variants alter six PAM-interacting residues of the PI domain
readout: log10 HT-PAMDA cleavage rate constant on the NAAA PAM
assay_method: High-throughput PAM determination assay (HT-PAMDA): each SpCas9 variant is incubated with a library of randomized-PAM substrates and cleavage is followed over time by sequencing, giving a first-order rate constant per PAM. Variants come from bacterial selections on a range of target PAMs and from random sampling of the SpCas9(6AA) library.
remark: The reference sequence is UniProt Q99ZW2 unmodified, and residues 1135, 1136, 1218, 1219, 1335 and 1337 read DSGERT, which is the code the source data itself uses for wild-type SpCas9. Enzymes are named in the source by a six-letter code over those positions and are converted to substitution labels against the wild type, a letter equal to the wild-type residue contributing nothing; 16 codes were isolated independently two or three times across different bacterial selections and their measurements are averaged, agreeing to a median of 0.48 log10 units with a worst case of 3.85, which is the only reproducibility estimate the table offers. Supplementary Note 3 lists the six randomized positions as D1135, S1135, G1218, E1219, R1335 and T1337, naming 1135 twice; Supplementary Figure 7 gives 1135, 1136, 1218, 1219, 1335 and 1337, and Q99ZW2 reads S at 1136, so the figure's numbering is followed. Not extracted from this paper: the PAMmla predictions of Supplementary Table 2 and the 64 million predicted enzyme profiles, which are computed rather than assayed; and the GUIDE-seq2 results of Supplementary Table 6, which measure off-target editing at genomic sites rather than a fitness per enzyme variant. The article itself is paywalled and is not redistributed in papers/; the supplementary tables it draws on are open and are staged instead.

assay_method: High-throughput PAM determination assay (HT-PAMDA): each SpCas9 variant is incubated with a library of randomized-PAM substrates and cleavage is followed over time by sequencing, giving a first-order rate constant per PAM. Variants come from bacterial selections on a range of target PAMs and from random sampling of the SpCas9(6AA) library.
remark: The reference sequence is UniProt Q99ZW2 unmodified, and residues 1135, 1136, 1218, 1219, 1335 and 1337 read DSGERT, which is the code the source data itself uses for wild-type SpCas9. Enzymes are named in the source by a six-letter code over those positions and are converted to substitution labels against the wild type, a letter equal to the wild-type residue contributing nothing; 16 codes were isolated independently two or three times across different bacterial selections and their measurements are averaged, agreeing to a median of 0.48 log10 units with a worst case of 3.85, which is the only reproducibility estimate the table offers. Supplementary Note 3 lists the six randomized positions as D1135, S1135, G1218, E1219, R1335 and T1337, naming 1135 twice; Supplementary Figure 7 gives 1135, 1136, 1218, 1219, 1335 and 1337, and Q99ZW2 reads S at 1136, so the figure's numbering is followed. Not extracted from this paper: the PAMmla predictions of Supplementary Table 2 and the 64 million predicted enzyme profiles, which are computed rather than assayed; and the GUIDE-seq2 results of Supplementary Table 6, which measure off-target editing at genomic sites rather than a fitness per enzyme variant. The article itself is paywalled and is not redistributed in papers/; the supplementary tables it draws on are open and are staged instead.

protein: SaAmd, an amidase signature (AS) family amidase; variants at active-site loop L3 (207-210) and distal loop positions 123 and 364
readout: Specific activity (U/mg) for hydrolysis of 1-GSH, the glutathione conjugate of 7-acetamido-4-chloromethylcoumarin (AACMC), a amide substrate
assay_method: Purified enzyme assayed for hydrolysis of 1-GSH, the glutathione conjugate of 7-acetamido-4-chloromethylcoumarin (AACMC) under standard conditions (100 uM substrate, 50 mM Tris-HCl, 100 mM NaCl, 10 percent v/v DMSO, pH 7.5, 22-24 degC); specific activity in U/mg from the linear increase in fluorescence or absorbance of the hydrolysis product. The variants themselves were found by an ultrahigh-throughput fluorescence-activated cell sorting (FACS) screen of combinatorial SaAmd libraries, in which a coumarin hydrolysis product is retained inside the cell by glutathione conjugation via a coexpressed glutathione S-transferase, giving a stable genotype-phenotype link; this file reports the follow-up purified-enzyme measurements, not the sort itself.
remark: The reference sequence is UniProt A0A7H0LPJ3 (amidase from Sphingomonas alpina, SaAmd), 436 residues. The paper expresses it with a C-terminal LELEHHHHHH extension (446 residues in Supplementary Information); that tag is dropped here because it is a purification artefact appended after the native C-terminus and, being C-terminal, does not shift any residue number. All six mutated positions (S123, A207, R208, S209, V210, A364) verify against the sequence exactly. The wild-type row is a genuine measurement, not a synthesized 1.0: SaAmd WT was assayed alongside the variants in the same Table S3 panel and its specific activity is reported here as measured. Variant labels combining two or three substitutions are joined with ':' in the mutant column. This is one of eight datasets from this paper, one per substrate, sharing the same 20 variants and the same wild type; they differ only in which substrate the specific activity was measured against. As a check, three separate fold-improvements the paper states in prose re-derive from these files: the triple variant S123N:R208P:A364E reaches 16.4-fold over wild type on N-(4-nitrophenyl)benzamide against a stated 'up to 16-fold'; the double S209P:V210P reaches 4.7-fold on the same substrate against a stated 'almost 5-fold'; and the double R208S:S209Q reaches 5.6-fold on the ester 4-methylumbelliferyl acetate against a stated 'up to 6-fold'. Not extracted from this paper: the FACS sorting data itself (Figures S7-S8), which are population fluorescence distributions rather than per-variant scores; the library-composition tables (Table S2), which list what was randomized rather than what each variant did; and the PdAmd comparison (Figure S9), which is a different enzyme rather than a variant of this wild type.

protein: D-amino acid oxidase (DAOx), an FAD-dependent oxidase, assayed as an Aga2p surface-display fusion
readout: Expression-normalized activity fitness on D-alanine, relative to wild-type DAOx (fold, WT = 1)
assay_method: EP-Seq: DAOx variants displayed on Saccharomyces cerevisiae EBY100 as Aga2p fusions and assayed by single-cell tyramide/peroxidase proximity labeling of the H2O2 released from D-alanine at 7.3 mM, its Km, then sorted by FACS into four fluorescence bins with variant identity and abundance per bin read out by barcode Illumina sequencing. remark: The assayed construct is DAOx residues 1-365: UniProt P80324 continues with the peroxisomal targeting tripeptide SKL at 366-368, which the yeast-display construct replaces with a V5 and 6xHis fusion tail, as confirmed from DAOx_ref.fa in the Zenodo deposit of the earlier EP-Seq paper (10.5281/zenodo.8388902), and positions 2-365 were independently re-derived from the 5,800 mutation labels and agree with P80324 at every position. Not extracted from this paper: the ten Sp-score substrate-specificity columns, which are the authors' own z-scores of fitness differences and are a separate property; the expression fitness column, measured in the earlier paper; the synonymous and nonsense variants, which are not amino acid substitutions; and the single-clone Amplex Red validation (18 variants), the purified-enzyme kinetics (5 to 6 variants) and the Fig. 7C combinatorial set (15 variants), all under the 20-variant floor.

remark: The reference sequence is NCBI WP_011390153.1, the 466-residue Rhodospirillum rubrum Form II rubisco, and the residues the source states in its own position and WTresidue columns match it at all 462 covered positions with no offset. Taken from the publisher's Supplementary Data 2 rather than the GitHub deposit named in the data availability statement, and the two are separate runs of the paper's bootstrap rather than copies: GitHub carries nine mutants absent from the supplement (A77T, A179T, A179V, F126D, G110P, K310A, N111V, S368G, V24Q) plus a wild-type row, and on the 8,760 rows they share every Km_median, Vmax_median and coefficient-of-variation value differs slightly (median relative difference 0.9% for Km_median, 0.7% for Vmax_median). The supplement's 8,760 rows are the figure the paper itself reports as 'more than 99% (8,760 of 8,835)', and all three readouts curated here come from that one file so that a variant's fitness, velocity and affinity are the same bootstrap run. Not extracted from this paper: the apparent CO2 affinity K_C, which is a different quantity needing its own directory and a quality filter -- the paper estimates it for only 65% of variants, and Km_qbcov <= 1.0 reproduces its stated 5,687 exactly as 5,686 mutants plus the wild type; the nine per-replicate enrichment columns, which the Fitness column summarizes; the literature and in vitro kinetics of Supplementary Data 1, which are other laboratories' measurements and mostly cover homologues rather than this library; and the ProteinGym files in the GitHub deposit, which are other publications' data that this paper evaluates against.

protein: EnvZ, the osmosensing histidine kinase (DHp domain mutated, positions 230-289)
readout: Reporter activation at 30 C (Gaussian fit mean of the +signal GFP fluorescence distribution, arbitrary units)
assay_method: Single-site saturation mutagenesis of the EnvZ DHp domain (NNS codons at each of positions 230-289) in Escherichia coli carrying a GFP reporter downstream of EnvZ's cognate response regulator OmpR, so that reporter expression tracks OmpR phosphorylation and hence EnvZ kinase activity. Cells were grown at 30 C and sorted by fluorescence into bins; per-variant bin frequencies from three replicates were normalised by the fraction of cells sorted into each bin and fitted with a bimodal Gaussian, the mean of the larger peak being the reported score.
remark: Assembled from the authors' MaveDB deposit (urn:mavedb:00001240-a-1, CC0), which the paper's data availability statement names, rather than from the article: the version of record is CC-BY but cell.com refuses automated retrieval, so only the deposit is staged in original_datasets/ and every statement below rests on MaveDB's own metadata rather than on the paper's methods section. The deposited target is the 60-residue EnvZ DHp domain and its labels are numbered 1-60 within it. Those 60 residues were located in UniProt P0AEJ4, the 450-residue Escherichia coli K-12 EnvZ, by exact string match at residues 230-289 -- the positions the deposit itself names -- so every label here carries the full-length numbering, +229 on the deposited one, and the sequence is the whole protein rather than the mutated domain. The wild-type residue of all 1201 labels was checked against that sequence with no mismatch. The readout is the deposit's own score column, which MaveDB designates as the score and whose method text describes as the mean of the larger Gaussian fitted to the variant's +signal fluorescence distribution across three sorting replicates. Higher is already better: more reporter activation means more phosphorylated OmpR and so more EnvZ kinase activity. This is an indirect readout -- GFP expression downstream of the cognate regulator, not a direct kinetic measurement -- and it is not baseline-subtracted. The 37 C arm of the same experiment (urn:mavedb:00001240-a-3) is deliberately not curated. Its score column fails the experiment's own internal control: the 59 nonsense variants truncate the kinase and must be dead, and at 30 C and 42 C they are -- median 2.26 and 2.15 against a wild type of 3.73 in both -- but at 37 C their median is 3.754 against a wild type of 3.639, so a truncated EnvZ scores higher than the intact one. Half the substitutions (556 of 1,122) fall on the dead side of that median, which is what a column carrying no signal looks like. fold_induction does not rescue it: it separates wild type (73.3) from nonsense (1.18) there, but puts the median substitution at 1.16, indistinguishable from dead, which would make almost every mutation lethal at 37 C and contradict the paper's own finding of high mutational tolerance. The 37 C file is also the only one of the three carrying full float precision rather than values rounded to two decimals, so it appears to have been processed differently. Without the article's methods -- unreachable, see above -- that cannot be resolved, so it is left out rather than shipped: it would have passed every check in this repository. Not extracted: mean_off, std_on and std_off, the fitted mean and widths of the -signal distribution; and fold_induction, the on/off ratio. fold_induction would be the baseline-controlled quantity and is arguably the better readout, but it is not the deposit's designated score, and it does not equal 10**(score - mean_off) across the file (112 of 1201 rows), so what it is exactly cannot be established without the paper's methods. Recorded here rather than guessed at. Rows dropped: 60 nonsense variants, whose Ter label is not a substitution this format can express. The one synonymous entry, p.Leu1Leu, is the wild type and is kept as the WT row, which is where wt_readout comes from. The score is clamped at both ends: it never leaves 0.8-4.7 in any of the three temperatures, and in this one 10 rows sit at exactly 0.8 and 4 at exactly 4.7. Those are the limits of the sorting range rather than measured values, so the extremes of this column are censored and a variant at 0.8 should be read as 'at or below the floor', not as a measurement. Note also that the MaveDB record's linked publication is 10.1073/pnas.2221163120, an earlier paper from the same laboratory; the DOI recorded here is the Cell Reports paper whose data availability statement names this accession.

protein: NucB, the secreted biofilm-dispersing nuclease
readout: Enrichment factor in generation g1 (sorted output frequency / input frequency)
assay_method: Ultra-high-throughput droplet screen of a designed NucB variant library: variants were expressed, incubated with a fluorogenic DNA substrate whose cleavage releases signal, sorted by fluorescence, and the sorted and input populations deep-sequenced. The readout is the enrichment factor of each genotype at the sort 3, high gate of generation g1, one round of an iterative machine-learning-guided design campaign (TeleProt).
remark: The wild type is the 142-residue NucB nuclease of Bacillus licheniformis as the deposit itself prints it; the repository's own alignment file is named F1BV52_BACLI, and UniProt F1BV52, the Bacillus licheniformis NucB, is byte-identical to it over all 142 residues, so the construct needed no reconstruction and carries no tag or truncation. Every genotype in this file was re-derived by applying the deposit's own mutation tuples to that sequence, and each was required to name the residue actually present at its position. Curated from the authors' public deposit rather than the article. github.com/google-deepmind/nuclease_design (Apache-2.0) points at a public bucket, storage.googleapis.com/nuclease_design, whose processed_data/g1.csv is the source here; the Cell Systems paper itself is CC-BY but cell.com refuses it to an automated fetch, so its methods section is unread and every statement here rests on the deposit. The readout is an enrichment factor -- the variant's frequency in the sorted output over its frequency in the input -- so higher is already better and no inversion was needed. One gate of several, chosen on the numbers. This generation was sorted at more than one stringency, and the columns are not equivalent: the most stringent gates recover almost nothing and collapse, g3's 99th-percentile gate being zero for 16,530 of 18,618 variants and g4's 99.5th for 14,027 of 15,404, both of them failing to separate the variants the deposit itself labels as beating wild type. This file uses ef_3_high_g1 (sort 3, high gate), which among this generation's gates has the fewest zeros and the most distinct values while still separating those labels (7.90 against 0.00 at the median). The other gates of this generation are left unshipped rather than averaged, because a mean across stringencies is not a quantity the experiment measured. Zeros are censored, not measured. 5,473 of 9,441 rows here are exactly 0, meaning the variant was never observed in the sorted output rather than that its activity was measured as nothing. They are kept, because dropping them would bias the file toward variants that survived selection, but a zero should be read as 'at or below detection'. Not extracted: the other enrichment gates of this generation and every gate of the other three, which are separate datasets here; the raw per-bin read counts the same columns are computed from; the p-values and the activity_greater_than_* calls, which are the deposit's own significance tests rather than measurements; and processed_data/landscape.csv, the 55,760-row summary the paper headlines, whose activity_level column is a four-level ordinal (non-functional / activity > 0 / activity > WT / activity > A73R) and so carries far less information per variant than the enrichment factors curated here.
